articles.title: Wolff tells critics to ‘watch Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse not F1’ as he defends Mercedes’ strategy
articles.summary: Principal denies bias towards Antonelli over Russell. Verstappen takes pole in sprint qualifying in Singapore. Toto Wolff has condemned accusations of bias in how he has managed his drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, with the Mercedes team principal describing those positing such theories…
body: With Antonelli leading Russell by 84 points in the world championship as they go into this weekend’s Singapore Grand Prix, the Italian’s first title is within his reach. The 20-year-old has driven superbly in only his second season in F1 but Russell has struggled with poor fortune and reliability issues that have stymied his championship challenge.

At the last round, in Malaysia, an engine failure cost Russell a potential podium spot and led to a host of accusations online of bias towards Antonelli. Speaking in Singapore, Wolff’s exasperation was clear.

“They’re brainless, whoever thinks that, it’s completely nonsensical,” he said. “I don’t know what’s going on. Do they think I have a button that says: ‘George, engine failure now’? Or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we are fighting for a constructors’ championship when we have always had the mindset of providing everybody equal material?

articles.title: Double moves Andrew Balding clear of Aidan O’Brien in Flat trainers’ race
articles.summary: Winners at Newmarket and York lift Balding’s spirits. Never So Brave wins Challenge Stakes at Newmarket. Andrew Balding’s late run at a first success in the Flat trainers’ championship gained extra momentum as an across-the-cards double, including a 1-2 in the Group Two Challenge Stakes, carried…
body: Balding was still around £700,000 adrift of O’Brien, the defending champion, at the end of August but has made steady progress since and moved into the lead for the first time when Blue Bolt won the Group One Sun Chariot Stakes at Newmarket last weekend.

Never So Brave’s defeat of his stable companion, Flora Of Bermuda, in the Challenge Stakes was worth a total of £129,000, less than half an hour after Balding’s juvenile Nakila Sun had made all in the British EBF Final at York, which was worth £51,000 to the winner.

O’Brien then had to settle for second place in the Group One Fillies’ Mile here, as his runner Haven was overhauled inside the final furlong by the odds-on favourite, Musical Times, with Balding’s runners, Forbidden Fire and Scommessa Sicura, picking up minor place money in third and fifth.

“I’ve been at the sales all week, but I’d imagine the team at home are pretty pumped for it,” Balding said after his Challenge Stakes success. “If we’re still the same after Champions Day then I’ll start to get excited, but I wouldn’t dare say it will be.”

articles.title: Will anyone stop re-election of Infantino as Fifa president?
articles.summary: Little more than two months since news broke of Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, the chances appear slim that Gianni Infantino might be removed as president.
body: Remember when pretty much everyone thought Gianni Infantino's days were numbered as Fifa president?
Infantino, who had seemed impregnable as the head of world football's governing body, suddenly appeared not only to be vulnerable, but in fact in an untenable position.
Yet, with 40 days to go until the 18 November deadline for nominations for the presidential election, senior figures in world football now firmly believe the 56-year-old may well be unopposed.
Uefa thought that FFE had given it the chance to cut the head off the snake.

articles.title: Maresca maintains almost total control as he follows Manchester City owners’ line | Jamie Jackson
articles.summary: Manager’s media conference was three times busier than usual, but he and his club are still speaking with one voice – for now. Enzo Maresca’s first public display since Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules was controlled – apart from…
body: In Thursday’s pre-emptive PR move, the club had Maresca tell their channels that he was aware of the “noise” around City. Fast forward 24 hours, and to a packed media conference of 45 attendees – around a threefold increase on the norm – at the Etihad Campus, the Italian was asked if this was dismissive of the anger felt towards the club’s cheating. “I understand the reason why most of you are here but the only thing I can say is that there is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club,” he replied.

This correspondent’s radar bleeped at the use of “in this moment” and, when the microphone was passed, Maresca was quizzed if this meant he may change his mind. “Sorry, that was the wrong answer. I completely trust the club in this moment, in the future, always.” But there was no denying the initial response and how this points to these shaky times for all at City.

articles.title: Mike Ditka, legendary Chicago Bears head coach, dies aged 86
articles.summary: Hall of Famer led 1985 Bears to Super Bowl title. Coach was known for tough, gruff demeanor. The Super Bowl Shuffle to SNL: a life in pictures. Mike Ditka, who won NFL titles as a player and coach with the Chicago Bears, has died at 86, his family announced Friday.
body: “It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka,” the family said. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.”

Nicknamed “Iron Mike” as a player, Ditka helped revolutionize the tight end position, then moved to the sidelines and took over as Chicago’s coach. His 1985 Bears team featured one of football’s most dominant defenses ever. It also had enough outsized personalities to record a rap video, The Super Bowl Shuffle, and back up their boasting in the championship game three months later.
After retiring as a coach, Ditka became a restaurateur, pitchman and TV personality, as well as an advocate for improved medical and retirement benefits for former players.

articles.title: Decision to stay at Celtic did not take long - O'Neill
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill suggests he was never close to leaving Celtic after a three-game losing streak, with the veteran manager stressing his "great enthusiasm" for the role.
body: The 74-year-old signed a one-year deal to stay on as manager after two interim spells last season culminated in a league and Scottish Cup double.
Following two defeats by Rangers last month - either side of a 3-1 home defeat by Ferencvaros in the Europa League - O'Neill felt "it might be time to wrap it up".
However, he said the decision to carry on "didn't take that long" as he prepared for Sunday's Premiership visit to Motherwell.
"Obviously, I'm disappointed with the week that we had," he explained. "As long as the football club wanted me, I was happy to do it."

articles.title: Lions' Dan Campbell recalls 'intimidating' interview with Mike Ditka
articles.summary: Dan Campbell had just finished his college football career at Texas A&M and was getting ready for the NFL draft when he met Mike Ditka for the first time. A promising tight end prospect who would go on to be a third-round pick in the 1999 draft, Campbell was at the NFL combine that winter when he…
body: Ditka, the first tight end ever inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, was in his final year as Saints coach after an iconic run with the Chicago Bears. Campbell figured he'd get to meet Ditka and several others at the meeting, but when he walked into the Saints' combine interview room he was in for a surprise.

"I go in and there’s one little light on," Campbell recalled Friday, Oct. 9. "It’s like a little lamp in the corner. It’s at the train station, and there’s nothing in there. There’s no couches. The room is totally cleaned out and there’s one little table, and the room is full of smoke. I mean, you can’t hardly even see him. You just see this image off in the corner, this little lamp and smoke everywhere and he’s got that big, fat cigar. And it was – it was one of the best times of my life and most intimidating times of my life sitting across from Mike Ditka."

He won Rookie of the Year and became the first tight end ever to top 1,000 yards receiving in a season in 1961, played for the Bears' NFL championship team in 1963 and led the organization to its last Super Bowl title in 1985 as a coach.

articles.title: Afcon move to every four years under review by Caf
articles.summary: The Africa Cup of Nations may continue to be held every two years, with discussions under way to reverse its proposed switch to a four-year cycle.
body: Speaking on Friday at a Confederation of African Football (Caf) strategy conference in Cape Verde, president Patrice Motsepe said: "We've discussed it over the last few days.
"We are looking at everything, including having the Afcon coming back every two years. We are very clear, the matter is being reviewed."
The tournament has taken place every two years since 1968, bar a one-year gap between the 2012 and 2013 editions.
However, in December 2025 CAF announced it would shift to being staged every four years after the 2027 Afcon in East Africa and a 2028 edition.

articles.title: Mike Ditka and his Bears teams have memorable history with Packers
articles.summary: Tensions during the Bears-Packers rivalry were high, and rightfully so, during the era when the late Mike Ditka was head coach of the Chicago Bears.
body: Chicago Bears legend Mike Ditka died Friday at age 86, leaving behind a legacy as a Hall of Fame player and Super Bowl-champion coach.

He oversaw the Bears as head coach from 1982 to 1992, a time when the Green Bay Packers were well behind the Bears in the NFL pecking order – not that it diminished the bad blood between the franchises.

The Bears have inched ahead of Green Bay over the past couple seasons, with another matchup looming Sunday, Oct. 11, though Green Bay's dominance in the rivalry began in 1992 with the arrival of Brett Favre and Ditka's departure.
Of the 10 full seasons he coached with the Bears, Ditka had only two losing seasons. Starting in 1983, the Packers won only five times in 20 meetings with Ditka's Bears.

articles.title: Antonelli casts further doubt over performance of Mercedes upgrades
articles.summary: World Championship leader Kimi Antonelli cast further doubt over the performance of Mercedes' recent upgrade package as he explained his car was "very difficult" to drive during Sprint Qualifying in Singapore.
body: After the long-awaited upgrades failed to deliver improved performance when they debuted at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Mercedes decided to compare different specifications of the car in Singapore.

Antonelli is running the latest version, which included an additional front wing that had not been available in Malaysia, while George Russell is running the pre-Malaysia version of the car that he won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in last month.

The early evidence was concerning for Mercedes as Russell finished second to Max Verstappen in the shortened qualifying session, with Antonelli more than half a second down on his team-mate in seventh.
Asked whether he was surprised by the performance, Antonelli said: "Yes and no, to be fair. Already in FP1 I was struggling.

articles.title: 'I only found out this morning' - Moyes surprised Everton are up for sale
articles.summary: David Moyes has admitted his surprise at Everton being put up for sale by owners The Friedkin Group - even claiming he only found out on Friday morning when the statement was released to the supporters.
body: The Friedkin Group (TFG) announced they are open to new investment into the club - including the "potential sale of a controlling interest".
The group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin, only completed their full takeover of Everton in December 2024 - ending Farhad Moshiri's long spell at the helm.

"Yeah I was surprised, they'd only came in a year and a half ago," Moyes said in a press conference - before claiming he first felt signs of the owners not being committed during the most recent transfer window.
"Most owners come in for a lot longer than that. We were all expecting them to be here for 20 to 30 years, however long it may be.
